sentiment_score_definition: x <= -0.35: Bearish; -0.35 < x <= -0.15: Somewhat-Bearish; -0.15 < x < 0.15: Neutral; 0.15 <= x < 0.35: Somewhat_Bullish; x >= 0.35: Bullish
relevance_score_definition: 0 < x <= 1, with a higher score indicating higher relevance.

feed.title: Devin Nunes officially resigns from Congress, clearing way to helm Trump's social media company
feed.summary: Devin Nunes officially resigned from Congress to become CEO of former President Trump's media and technology company, Truth Social. Nunes, a staunch ally of Trump, will lead the new platform which aims to be an alternative to mainstream social media. His move signifies his continued loyalty to Trump and his transition from a congressional career focused initially on local issues to national security and defense of the former president.

feed.title: Qualcomm, Microsoft partner on metaverse chip for AR glasses
feed.summary: Qualcomm and Microsoft are collaborating on custom chips for lightweight augmented reality (AR) glasses, targeting both consumers and businesses for metaverse applications. The partnership aims to integrate these chips with Microsoft's Mesh software for virtual presence and Qualcomm's Snapdragon Spaces for AR functions like spatial mapping and hand-tracking. Though no release date was provided, the initiative seeks to advance wearable AR devices for broader adoption.

feed.title: What Crypto-related ETFs Could Hit the US Market in 2022?
feed.summary: The article discusses the potential for various crypto-related ETFs, particularly metaverse products, to launch in the US market in 2022, while the approval of spot bitcoin and ether futures products remains uncertain. Industry experts express apprehension about the immediate investability of metaverse ETFs due to potential crossover in holdings and a lack of pure-play names. There's also skepticism regarding the SEC's approval of a spot bitcoin ETF in 2022, with some analysts expecting an ether futures-based ETF to gain approval sooner.

feed.title: P&G takes first step into the metaverse with BeautySphere
feed.summary: P&G Beauty has entered the metaverse with the launch of BeautySphere, a virtual storytelling world accessible via desktop, which debuted at CES. This platform enables consumers to interact with P&G's brands through live content, panel discussions, and gamified challenges, focusing on the company's "Responsible Beauty" initiatives. BeautySphere aims to engage digitally-savvy consumers on a nascent virtual landscape, bridging virtual experiences with real-world impact, such as planting trees for reforestation efforts.

feed.title: Trump’s social media app to launch in February, App Store listing says
feed.summary: Donald Trump's new social media app, Truth Social, is set to launch on February 21, 2022, according to an Apple App Store listing. The launch comes 13 months after Trump was banned from major social media platforms like Facebook and Twitter. The app will offer features similar to Twitter and is the first of three planned stages for the Trump Media & Technology Group (TMTG), which also plans a subscription video service and a podcast network.

feed.title: Meta leases up all office space in Austin's tallest tower in historic deal
feed.summary: Meta Platforms Inc., the parent company of Facebook, has leased all 589,000 square feet of office space at Sixth and Guadalupe, which will be Austin's tallest building. This historic deal ends months of speculation and signifies Meta's commitment to expand its presence in Austin, with plans to hire hundreds more employees in the city. The company will also maintain its existing downtown Austin offices.

feed.title: Tech Moves: Adaptive CFO to resign; Meta comms exec departs; AI vet joins Absci board; new Zymeworks CEO
feed.summary: This article details several significant personnel changes in the tech and biotech sectors, including Chad Cohen's resignation as CFO of Adaptive Biotechnologies, Joseph Sirosh's appointment to the Absci board, John Pinette's departure from Meta, and Kenneth Galbraith becoming the new CEO of Zymeworks. It highlights the impact of these moves on the respective companies and their financial performance or strategic direction.

feed.title: Meta Platforms adds DoorDash CEO Tony Xu to board of directors
feed.summary: Meta Platforms has announced that DoorDash CEO Tony Xu has been appointed to its board of directors. Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg praised Xu for building a successful service for millions of people and numerous businesses. Xu co-founded DoorDash in 2013 at Stanford University.

feed.title: Exercise by Accident: VR Games To Help You Work Out at Home
feed.summary: This article highlights how virtual reality (VR) games can offer a fun and effective way to exercise at home, even for those who find traditional workouts challenging. It categorizes various VR games into dedicated fitness apps, rhythm-based games, action titles, sporty simulations, and training programs, detailing how each can contribute to physical activity and fitness goals. The piece also mentions Oculus Move, a system-level fitness tracker, to monitor calorie burn across VR apps and encourages readers to share their favorite VR exercise routines.

feed.title: Facebook faces $3.2 bln UK class action over market dominance
feed.summary: Facebook, now Meta Platforms, is facing a £2.3 billion ($3.2 billion) class-action lawsuit in the UK for allegedly abusing its market dominance by exploiting the personal data of 44 million users between 2015 and 2019. The lawsuit, brought by Liza Lovdahl Gormsen, claims Facebook imposed unfair terms requiring users to surrender valuable personal data to access its network. This legal challenge comes shortly after Facebook lost an attempt to strike out an antitrust lawsuit from the Federal Trade Commission in the U.S.

feed.title: Facebook loses bid to dismiss users’ data-privacy antitrust claims
feed.summary: A California federal judge has partially denied Facebook's motion to dismiss antitrust claims from consumers and advertisers, allowing complaints regarding false data privacy representations and an agreement with Google to proceed. While certain claims against Meta Platforms Inc. were dismissed, plaintiffs have been granted 45 days to refile amended complaints. This decision follows another recent ruling against Facebook in an antitrust case filed by the Federal Trade Commission.

feed.title: A Guide to Investing in Emerging Asian Markets Outside of China
feed.summary: This article discusses investment opportunities in five emerging Asian markets—Pakistan, Bangladesh, Indonesia, Vietnam, and the Philippines—dubbed "Asian Growth Cubs" by Dawn Global Management. These countries offer significant growth potential for investors looking for exposure to Asian markets outside of China and India, with a collective GDP similar to India's but a much lower market cap. The article highlights the Asian Growth Cubs ETF (CUBS) as a way for foreign investors to access these markets, focusing on industries like healthcare, telecom, and technology.

feed.title: Meta Platforms: Roundhill Ball Metaverse ETF - Symbol Change Option Symbol: META New Symbol: METV
feed.summary: This document announces a symbol change for Meta Platforms (META) related to the Roundhill Ball Metaverse ETF. The old symbol for the option was META, and the new symbol is METV.

feed.title: Certification programs build digital skills
feed.summary: The Economic Development Corporation Michigan City (EDCMC) and Goodwill Industries of Michiana are collaborating to offer certification programs for digital skill enhancement. These online courses, including Facebook Social Media Marketing and Google IT Support, aim to help community members earn stackable certificates in high-demand fields. The programs are designed to assist individuals in overcoming barriers to education and employment by providing coursework, mentorship, and job placement services.

feed.title: Mother sues Meta and Snap over tween daughter’s suicide
feed.summary: An American mother has filed a lawsuit against Meta Platforms Inc. and Snap Inc., alleging their social media platforms, Instagram and Snapchat, are responsible for her 11-year-old daughter's suicide. The lawsuit claims the daughter developed an "extreme addiction" to these platforms, which the companies allegedly knew were harmful to minor users. This legal action comes amid increasing scrutiny and ongoing investigations into the mental health impact of social media on young people.

feed.title: Microsoft secures IPs like Call of Duty and Candy Crash to boost its metaverse ambitions, analyst says
feed.summary: Microsoft's $68.7 billion acquisition of Activision Blizzard is seen as a strategic move to bolster its metaverse ambitions, according to analyst Joost Rietveld. The deal secures popular gaming franchises like Call of Duty and Candy Crush, potentially differentiating Microsoft's Game Pass service and influencing cross-platform availability. While Microsoft has committed to honoring existing agreements, allowing Call of Duty to remain on PlayStation for now, the long-term impact on platform exclusivity for other IPs remains uncertain.

feed.title: What a Bristol-Myers project to monitor off-label prescribing says about future uses of A.I.
feed.summary: Bristol-Myers Squibb collaborated with Cortical.io to utilize AI for monitoring off-label drug prescribing by analyzing social media data. The pilot project successfully identified off-label uses of drugs, including an unexpected finding for Suboxone, demonstrating the potential of natural language processing and less data-intensive AI methods for post-market surveillance. This initiative highlights the growing importance of AI in patient safety and the value of brain-inspired AI research.

feed.title: The 3 Best Carbon Stocks of 2022
feed.summary: This article highlights the top three carbon-related investment opportunities for 2022, emphasizing the growing importance of carbon markets and green investing. It details the KraneShares Global Carbon Strategy ETF (KRBN) for broad market exposure, Carbon Streaming Corporation (NETZ/OFSTF) as an early mover in carbon credit streaming, and Brookfield Renewable Partners (BEP) for a more conservative renewable energy play. The article underscores how increasing net-zero ambitions among corporations and rising awareness of climate change will drive investor interest in these sectors.

feed.title: Fidelity kickstarts process to list metaverse and crypto company ETFs
feed.summary: Fidelity Investments has initiated the process with the SEC to launch two new exchange-traded funds (ETFs) targeting the crypto and metaverse sectors. The Crypto Industry and Digital Payments ETF will focus on companies involved in crypto mining, blockchain technology, and digital payments, while the Fidelity Metaverse ETF will track companies generating revenue from metaverse-related technologies. This development follows Fidelity's previous attempts to launch crypto-related investment products, including a rejected spot bitcoin ETF in the US and a Canadian Bitcoin ETF.

feed.title: Timing Is Everything For ETFs
feed.summary: Thematic ETFs, which invest in specific market themes, have grown significantly. Their success often depends heavily on the timing of their launch, sometimes due to unintentional events, as exemplified by the ETFMG Prime Cyber Security ETF (HACK) benefiting from major cybersecurity breaches shortly after its inception. Conversely, funds like the Sprott Buzz Social Media Insights ETF (BUZ) failed due to poor timing, while later similar entrants thrived by tapping into peak market interest.

feed.title: Morgan Stanley Sees $8 Trillion Metaverse Market — In China Alone
feed.summary: Morgan Stanley predicts an $8 trillion metaverse market in China alone, replacing the mobile internet with a more "immersive experience." The investment bank acknowledges significant technological and regulatory hurdles for mass adoption, estimating an initial total addressable market of $4 trillion before expanding to $8 trillion as it disrupts offline activities.

feed.title: Beer Summit Takeaways: A-B CEO Previews Bud Light Next; Digital Marketing Opportunities on Facebook, Instagram; Lots of Seltzer Talk
feed.summary: The article summarizes key discussions from Beer Business Daily’s Beer Industry Summit, detailing Anheuser-Busch InBev's CEO Brendan Whitworth's insights on Bud Light Next and e-commerce, Meta's Pablo Merheb's presentation on digital marketing for alcohol brands, and growth updates from Diageo’s Lone River Ranch Water, Molson Coors' Topo Chico Hard Seltzer, and Gopuff's expansion into beverage alcohol delivery. Constellation Brands CEO Bill Newlands also provided updates on the company’s Mexican import portfolio and Fresca Mixed.

feed.title: Amazon and Microsoft led the world in corporate purchases of clean energy in 2021
feed.summary: Amazon and Microsoft were global leaders in corporate clean energy power purchase agreements in 2021, with Amazon holding the top spot for the second consecutive year. Combined, the two tech giants procured 12.4 GW of wind and solar power, contributing significantly to a record-setting year for corporate carbon-free energy deals. Both companies are committed to achieving 100% renewable energy for their operations by 2025, with Microsoft aiming for 24/7 clean energy by 2030.

feed.title: Meta Reports Fourth Quarter and Full Year 2021 Results
feed.summary: Meta Platforms, Inc. reported solid financial results for the fourth quarter and full year 2021, driven by continued growth in user engagement and business use of its services. The company highlighted significant investments in key growth areas such as Reels, commerce, and virtual reality, alongside a new financial reporting structure separating its Family of Apps (FoA) and Reality Labs (RL) segments. Meta also announced its upcoming ticker symbol change to 'META' and provided an outlook for Q1 2022 revenue, anticipating headwinds from increased competition, platform changes, and macroeconomic factors.

feed.title: TMUS Stock: 9 Reasons Why T-Mobile Investors Are Dialing Up Gains Today
feed.summary: T-Mobile US (TMUS) stock is experiencing a significant surge after the telecommunications company released its fourth-quarter 2021 earnings report. Despite a slight revenue miss, diluted earnings per share surpassed Wall Street expectations, and a strong 2022 outlook, including projections for 5 million to 5.5 million postpaid net customer additions and significant merger synergies, contributed to investor optimism. The positive report has led to heavy trading activity, with TMUS stock up over 10% as of Thursday afternoon.

feed.title: Document
feed.summary: Amazon.com, Inc. announced its financial results for the fourth quarter and full year ended December 31, 2021, showing increased net sales but decreased operating cash flow due to higher costs. The company reported a significant net income increase in Q4 2021, boosted by a valuation gain from its investment in Rivian Automotive. Amazon also highlighted continued investments in Prime benefits, expansion of AWS services, and initiatives in environmental protection and community support.

feed.title: Amazon raises Prime membership fees to offset growing costs
feed.summary: Amazon announced it is increasing its Prime membership fees in the United States to offset rising shipping costs and wages, despite exceeding profit expectations for the holiday quarter. The annual membership fee will go up to $139 from $119, effective February 18 for new members. The company's shares saw a significant rise following the announcement, although it also forecast first-quarter sales below Wall Street estimates.

feed.title: Warren Buffett’s Berkshire Hathaway Is Now Bigger Than Meta
feed.summary: Warren Buffett's Berkshire Hathaway has surpassed Meta Platforms in market capitalization, marking a significant shift in stock-market standing. This article highlights Berkshire Hathaway's increasing valuation relative to Meta.

feed.title: H&R Block rolls out mobile banking in time for tax season
feed.summary: H&R Block has launched a new mobile banking service called Spruce, in partnership with Meta Financial’s MetaBank, to attract and serve clients, particularly those without traditional bank accounts. The service offers a spending account, debit card, mobile app, and savings features to help customers manage their finances and budget for specific goals. Spruce aims to address the financial health of many Americans, especially during tax season, by providing a low-to-no-fee banking product that facilitates direct deposit of tax refunds and offers features like early paycheck access and fee-free overdraft protection.

feed.title: Metaverse stocks Nvidia and Roblox fall as Facebook parent Meta's Web3 business reports massive loss
feed.summary: Shares of metaverse-related companies like Roblox, Nvidia, and Matterport fell after Meta Platforms reported a significant operating loss of $10 billion in its Web3 division, Reality Labs, for 2021. The news led to a market value wipeout of over $200 billion for Meta and a sell-off across various tech stocks connected to the metaverse concept. This downturn highlights concerns following Meta's aggressive push into the metaverse space.

feed.title: Zuckerberg loses $29b in a day as Meta shares crash
feed.summary: Mark Zuckerberg's net worth plummeted by $29 billion in a single day after Meta Platforms Inc.'s stock experienced a record dive following a disappointing earnings forecast. Meta's shares fell 26%, wiping out over $200 billion in market value, the largest single-day loss for a US company. This decline pushed Zuckerberg to the twelfth spot on Forbes' real-time billionaires list, with analysts citing Apple's privacy changes and increased competition from rivals like TikTok and YouTube as contributing factors.

feed.title: Amazon set for historic market cap gain after Meta’s epic loss
feed.summary: Amazon is projected to add approximately $155 billion in market value if its stock's 11% pre-market gain holds, placing it among the top five single-day gains in U.S. stock market history. This surge follows strong performance in its cloud computing division and a price increase for Amazon Prime, counteracting fears sparked by Meta Platforms Inc.'s recent significant market cap loss. Amazon's expected gain comes after it experienced its own decline, losing $119 billion in market value the day prior due to Meta's earnings flop.

feed.title: Amazon share price surges 19% in post-market trading as company announces price hike in Prime membership
feed.summary: Amazon's stock surged 19% in post-market trading after the e-commerce giant reported better-than-expected profits and announced an increase in its Prime membership price. This rise, along with strong earnings from Snap and Pinterest, helped to alleviate concerns following Meta Platforms' significant stock crash. Despite the after-hours rebound, Amazon and Snap shares only returned to mid-January levels, highlighting the extent of a recent selloff.

feed.title: Meta Stock Drop Biggest in History – Apple App Tracking Transparency a Factor
feed.summary: Meta's stock plunged by 26% on Thursday, resulting in a US$251.3 billion loss in market value, making it the largest single-day stock drop in history. This significant decline was largely attributed to Apple's App Tracking Transparency (ATT) privacy policy changes, which have impacted Meta's advertising revenue. Mark Zuckerberg also acknowledged increased competition from platforms like TikTok and a shift towards short-form video as contributing factors.

feed.title: Meta Extended Its Buybacks Into January—Just Before the Stock Slid
feed.summary: Meta Platforms aggressively repurchased its stock in the fourth quarter of 2021 and continued these buybacks into January 2022. This occurred just prior to the release of the company's disappointing fourth-quarter earnings report. The earnings report subsequently caused a significant decline in Meta's stock price.

feed.title: TelevisaUnivision Hires Multimedia Ad Sales Execs | Next TV | Broadcasting+Cable
feed.summary: TelevisaUnivision has announced the hiring of two new senior multimedia ad sales executives, Rob McGovern and Richard Bertodatti, to bolster its sales efforts. McGovern will lead West Coast national sales, while Bertodatti will manage business with major media agencies and the Boston territory. Both will report to John Kozack, Executive VP of multimedia sales, with a focus on showcasing the company's unique opportunities to marketers and leveraging the power of Hispanic audiences.

feed.title: Meta rivalry with Apple inflamed as Facebook parent company share price plummets
feed.summary: Meta's stock price plummeted by 26%, wiping out approximately $220bn in market value, primarily due to "headwinds" caused by Apple's new iOS privacy changes. Mark Zuckerberg blamed these changes, which restrict advertisers' ability to target ads, estimating a $10bn impact on Meta's business. In contrast, other tech companies like Snap, Amazon, and Pinterest reported strong ad revenue or stock growth, indicating that Apple's privacy updates did not affect all companies equally.

feed.title: Traditional conglomerates such as GE, J&J and Toshiba are moving in a new direction
feed.summary: Traditional conglomerates like General Electric, Johnson & Johnson, and Toshiba are breaking up their companies to increase shareholder value and simplify management. This trend is driven by past financial difficulties and the complexities of their diversified operations. In contrast, modern tech giants like Amazon and Meta thrive as conglomerates by leveraging platform-based models and network effects, which offer a different approach to managing varied businesses.

feed.title: Opinion: $1.4 trillion? Big Tech’s pandemic year produces mind-boggling financial results
feed.summary: In 2021, despite supply-chain disruptions, labor shortages, and rising prices, major tech companies including Alphabet, Amazon, Apple, Meta, and Microsoft achieved staggering financial results. They collectively saw over $320 billion in profit on $1.4 trillion in sales, with profits increasing more than 55% and sales growing 27% from an already record-setting base. This performance highlights Big Tech's resilience and expanding economic influence, making their combined sales comparable to a top-15 global economy.

feed.title: Amazon hiking base salary cap to $350,000 for corporate, tech workers
feed.summary: Amazon has announced a significant increase in its base salary cap for corporate and tech workers, raising it from $160,000 to $350,000. This move aims to enhance the company's competitiveness in a challenging labor market and attract and retain top talent. The company indicated that these increases are "much more considerable" than in previous years, aligning its pay structure more closely with other major tech firms.

feed.title: Peter Thiel to leave Meta board to pursue Trump political agenda
feed.summary: Peter Thiel, a long-serving board member of Meta Platforms Inc. and early investor in Facebook, is stepping down from the company's board after its annual shareholder meeting in May. Thiel intends to focus on increasing his political support for former President Donald Trump's agenda during the 2022 election, aiming to avoid being a "distraction" for Meta. He plans to back Republican candidates like Blake Masters and JD Vance who align with Trump's political aims.

feed.title: The metaverse is ‘particularly hard to predict,’ says Unity’s AR/VR chief
feed.summary: Timoni West, Unity's AR/VR chief, believes that while the excitement around spatial computing and the metaverse is justified, the exact future applications are "particularly hard to predict." She draws parallels to the early days of the internet, where people correctly envisioned themes like online shopping but failed to foresee the ultimate form it would take. West suggests that current attempts to apply existing patterns to new technologies, such as realistic avatars in virtual spaces, will likely evolve into something completely different over time.

feed.title: Peter Thiel to step down from board of Facebook parent Meta
feed.summary: Tech billionaire Peter Thiel is stepping down from the board of Meta Platforms Inc., the parent company of Facebook. Thiel, who co-founded PayPal and was an early investor in Facebook, has served on the board since 2015 and will not seek re-election at the company's annual stockholders meeting in May.

feed.title: Aussie funds exposed to the Meta rout: Charts of the Week
feed.summary: Australian managed funds and popular index-tracking ETFs, including those from Magellan, Hyperion, and Lakehouse, were significantly impacted by Meta Platforms' sharp 26% stock drop, the largest one-day market capitalization loss in US history. This "Meta rout" contributed to new year woes for growth investors, although some losses were mitigated by strong performance from Amazon.com positions within several of these funds. Sustainable funds generally avoided the Meta selloff due to ESG-related exclusions stemming from privacy concerns.

feed.title: Meta Is Now Calling Out Google Over Apple's App Privacy Rules
feed.summary: Meta Platforms Inc. is publicly criticizing Google, alleging it has an unfair advantage under Apple's new privacy policies. While Meta's apps must ask users for tracking consent, Google's search and browser functions do not, leading to a shift in advertiser budgets towards Google. This comes after Meta's revenue took a multibillion-dollar hit due to its inability to gather as much data on iPhone users.

feed.title: Better Buy: Meta Platforms vs. PayPal Holdings
feed.summary: This article compares Meta Platforms and PayPal Holdings after both companies experienced significant stock price drops due to disappointing earnings reports and future guidance. It outlines the reasons behind their respective crashes, including Apple's privacy changes and TikTok competition for Meta, and supply chain issues and increased competition for PayPal. The author ultimately argues that Meta is a more compelling investment due to its diversification, lower valuation, and wider moat, despite current risks for both stocks.

feed.title: Gartner: A quarter of consumers will use the metaverse daily by 2026
feed.summary: A Gartner report predicts that by 2026, 25% of consumers will spend at least one hour daily in the metaverse for various activities like work, shopping, or entertainment. The report advises organizations against over-investing in single metaverse components due to its early and disconnected stage of adoption but emphasizes the potential for digital currencies and immersive online events. Retailers are already engaging with the metaverse by partnering with platforms like Roblox and filing trademarks for virtual goods, while tech giants like Meta and Microsoft are investing heavily in its development.

feed.title: YouTube floats ideas of verifying NFTs, watching games in metaverse
feed.summary: YouTube is exploring using blockchain technology and NFTs to help creators find new ways to monetize content by offering verifiable digital assets. The company also suggested ideas for the metaverse, focusing on enhancing social viewing experiences, particularly for gaming content, to allow users to watch videos together in a virtual environment. These initiatives aim to cut down on fraud in the digital art market and improve user engagement.

feed.title: Qualcomm Expands XR & Metaverse Investment With The Formation of XR Labs Europe
feed.summary: Qualcomm Technologies has opened new Extended Reality (XR) Labs across six European cities to expand its investment in XR and the metaverse. These labs will focus on XR R&D, engineering, and key technology areas like hand tracking, 3D mapping, and multi-user experiences to make XR accessible and foster the Snapdragon Spaces XR Developer Platform. The initiative aims to support the development of lightweight head-worn devices and innovative experiences across various sectors, leveraging Europe's strong AR/VR community and Qualcomm's leadership in mobile and XR technology.

feed.title: Expedia CEO says the metaverse doesn’t pose a threat to what he calls ‘real-verse’ travel
feed.summary: Expedia CEO Peter Kern believes the metaverse does not pose a competitive threat to real-world travel, which he calls the "real-verse." While acknowledging the intrigue, Kern stated that virtual experiences cannot replicate the life-changing nature of physical travel to places like Paris or national parks. He expressed confidence that people will continue to prioritize real-world experiences, despite the growth in virtual reality investments.

feed.title: TikTok Inks Major Lease in Austin
feed.summary: TikTok has signed a major sublease for over 125,000 square feet at 300 Colorado, a 32-story high-rise in downtown Austin. The social media company will occupy the top six floors of the building, which was completed in 2021. This move comes as the Austin office market experienced significant activity, including a large lease by Meta Platforms, despite overall office vacancy remaining above the city's average.

feed.title: Stanley Druckenmiller Buys Chevron as Family Offices Reveal Stock Picks
feed.summary: Stanley Druckenmiller's Duquesne Family Office sold its Meta Platforms Inc. position and bought Chevron, indicating a shift away from big tech. Similarly, George Soros's family office reduced its stakes in Amazon.com, Alphabet, and a Nasdaq 100 ETF. These moves suggest a trend among some wealthy investors to re-evaluate their portfolios regarding large technology companies.

feed.title: Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton sues Facebook alleging social media giant violated state law
feed.summary: Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton has filed a lawsuit against Facebook's parent company, Meta Platforms, Inc., alleging that the social media giant violated state law by collecting and storing users' biometric information (facial features) from photos and videos without proper consent. The lawsuit claims Facebook shared this data and failed to destroy it in a timely manner, exposing millions of Texans to risks. Facebook has denied the claims, stating they are "without merit."

feed.title: Texas sues Facebook parent company over use of facial recognition technology
feed.summary: Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton has filed a lawsuit against Meta Platforms Inc., the parent company of Facebook, alleging violations of state privacy and anti-deceptive trade practice laws due to its past use of facial recognition technology. The suit claims Facebook failed to disclose biometric data collection, transmitted information to third parties, and did not delete data within a reasonable timeframe, seeking billions in damages. Meta has stated the claims are without merit and plans to defend itself vigorously, while political rivals have criticized Paxton's timing and use of outside counsel.

feed.title: Meta's Facebook to pay $90 million to settle privacy lawsuit over user tracking
feed.summary: Meta Platforms Inc (Facebook) has agreed to pay $90 million to settle a long-standing privacy lawsuit. The lawsuit accused Facebook of tracking users' internet activity, including visits to outside websites with "like" buttons, even after they logged out, and then compiling these browsing histories for advertisers. The settlement still requires court approval and mandates the deletion of improperly collected data, addressing claims of violating federal and state privacy and wiretapping laws.

feed.title: Facebook Stops Fighting Wiretap Act Litigation After More Than a Decade
feed.summary: Meta Platforms, Inc. (formerly Facebook) has proposed a $90 million national class action settlement in its long-running Facebook Internet Tracking Litigation, involving over 124 million Americans. The lawsuit stemmed from allegations that Facebook tracked user activity on non-Facebook sites using "Like" buttons between April 2010 and September 2011, violating federal and California Wiretap Act laws. While the settlement brings closure to a decade-long legal battle and requires deletion of old data, it also highlights potential future legal scrutiny for third-party trackers.

feed.title: Trump's new social media application 'Truth Social' begins gradual rollout
feed.summary: Donald Trump's "Truth Social" app began a gradual rollout on Sunday, with the aim of being fully operational in the US by the end of March. The platform is intended as an alternative to major social media sites that banned Trump after the January 6, 2021 Capitol assault. Former congressman Devin Nunes, CEO of Trump Media & Technology Group, stated that the app would be available on the Apple App Store, celebrating the return of free speech for those who felt their voices were canceled.

feed.title: HAGENS BERMAN, NATIONAL TRIAL ATTORNEYS, Alerts TaskUs, Inc. (TASK) Investors with Losses in Excess of $300K to Opportunity to Lead Securities Class Action
feed.summary: Hagens Berman, a national trial attorneys firm, is alerting TaskUs, Inc. (NASDAQ: TASK) investors who have significant losses to the opportunity to lead a securities class action lawsuit. The lawsuit alleges that TaskUs and its senior management made false and misleading statements about the company's content monitoring and moderation services, market size, and workforce metrics, leading to an drop in stock price after an analyst issued a "sell" opinion. The firm is seeking investors with losses exceeding $300,000 to come forward by the lead plaintiff deadline of April 25, 2022.

feed.title: How DBMS is Used by Hulu, JPMorgan Chase, and The Weather Company
feed.summary: This article examines how Database Management Systems (DBMS) are crucial for organizations to efficiently store, retrieve, and manage data. It provides case studies of how major companies like Hulu, JPMorgan Chase, and The Weather Company leverage DBMS to address challenges, optimize operations, and maintain data integrity and security, highlighting the benefits over traditional file systems. The article demonstrates the real-world applications and positive outcomes of integrating DBMS in various industries.

feed.title: 11 Inspiring Women Who Pivoted into Tech Careers After Completing 2U-Powered Boot Camps
feed.summary: This article highlights 11 women who successfully transitioned into tech careers after completing 2U-powered boot camps in various disciplines like coding, data science, cybersecurity, and fintech. The featured individuals come from diverse backgrounds, including full-time moms, mid-career pivoters, and those affected by pandemic layoffs. Their stories showcase how these boot camps equipped them with the skills needed to land new roles at companies such as Meta, Infosys, Johnson & Johnson, Lowe's, Citibank, and others, acting as role models and transforming the tech landscape.

feed.title: College could take place in the metaverse, but these problems must be overcome first
feed.summary: Higher education in the US faces significant challenges including rising tuition, student debt, and dissatisfaction with online learning. The metaverse could offer a solution by creating more immersive remote learning experiences, but it also presents new ethical and practical problems. Five key issues to address include ensuring academic freedom on private platforms, maintaining student focus in a highly distracting virtual environment, improving nonverbal communication through avatars, fostering a sense of community outside of physical campuses, and preventing new digital divides.

feed.title: Google, Meta face penalties in Russia as deadline passes to open local offices
feed.summary: Google and Meta are among several internet companies facing potential penalties in Russia for failing to establish local offices and comply with a new communications law. Russia's state communications regulator, Roskomnadzor, had set a deadline of the end of February for these companies to open local offices or face restrictions. The move is part of Russia's broader effort to control internet content, with fines previously issued for failing to censor anti-government content, and recent curtailments of access to platforms like Facebook in retaliation for censoring state media.

feed.title: Qualcomm Extends Connectivity Leadership with World's First and Fastest Wi-Fi 7 Commercial Solution
feed.summary: Qualcomm Technologies has introduced FastConnect 7800, the industry's first Wi-Fi 7 commercial solution, featuring High Band Simultaneous (HBS) Multi-Link technology for superior speeds and ultra-low latency. This advanced connectivity system also incorporates next-generation Intelligent Dual Bluetooth, enhancing Snapdragon Sound and Bluetooth LE Audio with improved range, faster pairing, and seamless device switching. The FastConnect 7800 is designed to deliver unparalleled wireless performance and power efficiency for a wide range of client devices.

feed.title: AMD, Arm, Google, Intel, TSMC and others join Universal Chiplet Interconnect Express (UCIe) group
feed.summary: Leading semiconductor companies including AMD, Arm, Google, Intel, Meta, Microsoft, Qualcomm, Samsung, and TSMC have formed the Universal Chiplet Interconnect Express (UCIe) industry consortium. This group aims to establish an open chiplet ecosystem by standardizing die-to-die interconnects, with the UCIe 1.0 specification already ratified. This initiative leverages existing PCI Express and Compute Express Link standards to enable easier mixing and matching of chiplet components from multiple vendors for System-on-Chip (SoC) construction.

feed.title: Apple, Netflix, TikTok strike back against Russian state media content
feed.summary: Several major tech and entertainment companies, including Apple, Netflix, and TikTok, are taking action against Russian state media and suspending services in Russia following the invasion of Ukraine. This includes Netflix refusing to carry Russian federal channels, Apple pausing product sales and limiting services, and social media platforms restricting access to and demoting content from outlets like RT and Sputnik due to concerns about propaganda and disinformation. The moves reflect a global condemnation of Russia's actions and a united front from U.S. businesses.

feed.title: Leaders in Semiconductors, Packaging, IP Suppliers, Foundries, and Cloud Service Providers Join Forces to Standardize Chiplet Ecosystem
feed.summary: A consortium of leading technology companies, including ASE, AMD, Arm, Google Cloud, Intel, Meta, Microsoft, Qualcomm, Samsung, and TSMC, has formed to standardize the chiplet ecosystem. They have ratified the Universal Chiplet Interconnect Express (UCIe) 1.0 specification, an open industry standard for die-to-die interconnects, aiming to enable multi-vendor compatibility for System-on-Chip construction. The consortium is open for membership and plans to develop future generations of the UCIe technology.

feed.title: Tripadvisor, Google Maps Suspend Reviews of Some Russian Listings
feed.summary: Google Maps and Tripadvisor have temporarily suspended new user reviews for certain listings in Russia, Ukraine, and Belarus. This action was taken in response to a flood of political statements posted as reviews, driven by a social media campaign urging activists to communicate with Russians via these platforms about the war in Ukraine. The companies aim to prevent the publishing of off-topic and abusive content.

feed.title: Universal Chiplet Interconnect Express (UCIe) group combines AMD, Arm, Google, Intel, TSMC and more
feed.summary: The Universal Chiplet Interconnect Express (UCIe) group, formed by major tech companies like AMD, Arm, Google, Intel, and TSMC, has established a new industry consortium. Their goal is to standardize die-to-die interconnect guidelines and foster an open chiplet ecosystem, developing the UCIe 1.0 specification for interoperable multi-vendor chiplet components. This initiative aims to drive innovation in customizable package-level integration and address future challenges in semiconductor systems.

feed.title: Spotify closes its office in Russia in response to attack on Ukraine
feed.summary: Spotify announced the indefinite closure of its office in Russia in response to the country's attack on Ukraine. The music streaming platform stated its priority is its employees' safety and ensuring access to information. Spotify has also restricted the discoverability of Russian state-affiliated media and removed content from RT and Sputnik in several markets, while matching employee donations for humanitarian aid.

feed.title: Goldman Sachs-Backed Virtual Beauty App Developer To Go Public In $1 Billion SPAC Deal
feed.summary: Perfect Corp., a Taiwan-headquartered virtual beauty try-on app developer backed by Goldman Sachs, announced its plan to go public in the U.S. through a SPAC merger valued at $1 billion. The combination with Nasdaq-listed Provident Acquisition Corp. is expected to raise up to $335 million, including a $50 million PIPE investment from investors like Chanel and Shiseido. CEO Alice Chang stated the company aims to expand into Southeast Asia and the Middle East, and further integrate its augmented reality technologies across more platforms and categories, including the metaverse.

feed.title: How Hyperscale Data Centers are reshaping India’s IT
feed.summary: Hyperscale data centers are critical infrastructure for companies like Amazon, Google, and Microsoft, providing dedicated computing resources to handle massive user demands. These facilities are essential for the digital economy, supporting everything from emails to online shopping, and their importance has grown with trends like remote work and emerging technologies such as AI and IoT. India is poised for significant growth in its data center industry, driven by government incentives and an increasing need for robust data storage and processing capabilities, despite environmental concerns related to energy consumption.

feed.title: The cloud over commercial real estate lingers
feed.summary: The commercial real estate market, particularly office spaces, continues to face challenges despite an initial return to optimism after the pandemic's early days. While some global forecasts are cautiously positive, the underlying issues of vacancy rates, decreasing property values, and the shift to remote work persist, leading to conversions of office spaces into residential units and increased incentives from landlords. The long-term impact on property valuations and investment returns remains a significant concern for the industry.

feed.title: Industry Leaders Join Forces to Standardize Chiplet Ecosystem
feed.summary: A consortium of industry leaders, including AMD, Arm, Google Cloud, Intel, Meta, Microsoft, Qualcomm, Samsung, TSMC, and ASE, has formed to standardize die-to-die interconnects and foster an open chiplet ecosystem. They have ratified the Universal Chiplet Interconnect Express (UCIe) 1.0 specification, an open industry standard for package-level connectivity. This initiative aims to reduce development time and cost, promoting customizable and interoperable chiplet designs for future silicon innovations.

feed.title: This CEO Has Purchased Over $1 Billion Worth Of His Own Stock Over The Last Year
feed.summary: Dustin Moskovitz, co-founder of Meta Platforms and Asana Inc., has made an aggressive insider stock purchase, buying over $1 billion worth of Asana shares since June 2021. He now owns more than 16.5 million shares, representing about 21% of the company. This comes as Asana, a SaaS company, experienced strong demand during the pandemic but has seen its stock price tumble recently.

feed.title: Blue Cross Blue Shield Owner Anthem Seeks to Rebrand to Elevance Health
feed.summary: Anthem Inc., owner of several Blue Cross Blue Shield plans, plans to rebrand as Elevance Health Inc. to reflect a broader business focus beyond traditional health insurance. The company has diversified into areas like behavioral health, home-based care, and data analytics, seeking to achieve a premium valuation similar to UnitedHealth Group. While the new name aims to resonate with Wall Street and employees, branding experts suggest it might be difficult to connect with consumers who will still encounter the Anthem brand through their health coverage.

feed.title: Biden must safeguard Russian internet access, civil society warns
feed.summary: Civil society groups are urging the Biden administration to protect internet providers in Russia from sanctions, arguing that cutting off web access would isolate dissidents and strengthen the Kremlin's control. They recommend that the Office of Foreign Asset Controls formally authorize U.S. internet services, software, and hardware to preserve web access, citing precedents from past sanctions campaigns. The groups warn that without clear guidance, individuals in Russia could be cut off from vital internet services.

feed.title: Grizzle Growth ETF (GRZZ) Stock Price, News, Quote & History
feed.summary: This article provides detailed information on the Grizzle Growth ETF (GRZZ), including its current stock price, historical data, and performance metrics. It outlines the ETF's investment strategy, top holdings like NVIDIA and Microsoft, and sector weightings. The page also features related ETF news and research reports from analysts regarding other companies.

feed.title: Russia says it will block Instagram
feed.summary: Russia announced it would block Instagram, blaming a recent change in Meta's hate-speech policy that temporarily allowed some users to call for violence against Russians in the context of the Ukraine war. This move is part of Russia's broader effort to control information flow and prevent its citizens from accessing uncensored news about the invasion. The ban is expected to affect 80 million Russian users.

feed.title: ‘The Dirty Dozen List’ – Corporations Enable and Profit from Sexual Exploitation
feed.summary: The National Center on Sexual Exploitation (NCOSE) has released its annual "Dirty Dozen List," highlighting twelve mainstream entities accused of facilitating and profiting from sexual abuse and exploitation. The list includes technology giants like Google, Meta, Discord, and others, pointing to various ways they enable access to harmful content or profit from commercial sex industries. NCOSE details specific examples for each company and offers ways for the public to take action against these practices.

feed.title: Metaverse Technology Redefining Digital Experience
feed.summary: The metaverse is emerging as a significant technological advancement, moving beyond gaming to redefine digital experiences across various industries. Companies like Facebook (Meta), Nike, and Microsoft are investing heavily, with projections indicating global metaverse revenue could approach $800 billion by 2024. While offering potential for retail, enterprise solutions, and new markets like virtual real estate and entertainment, the metaverse also faces challenges related to data security, legal frameworks, skilled resources, VR device limitations, and potential negative societal impacts.

feed.title: Russia to block Instagram over ‘death to invaders’ posting rule
feed.summary: Russia plans to block Instagram and has launched a criminal case against its owner, Meta Platforms Inc., following Meta's decision to allow posts calling for violence against Russian forces. This move comes as an escalation in Russia's confrontation with US-based social media platforms, with Moscow alleging that Instagram is spreading calls for violence against Russian citizens and military personnel. Meta has defended its decision as a temporary measure in extraordinary circumstances, aimed at protecting Ukrainians' freedom of speech in self-defense.

feed.title: Goldman Sachs CEO Says Ostracizing Russia Isn’t the Finance Industry’s Job
feed.summary: Goldman Sachs CEO David Solomon stated that it is not the finance industry's job to ostracize Russia, but rather to follow government sanctions. He emphasized that businesses should implement policies set by the government, agreeing with the sanctions against Russia's actions in Ukraine. Despite this stance, the article highlights Goldman Sachs's historical involvement in Russia's economic policy and its mixed record on activism.

feed.title: Aptos raises $200M to bring the Diem blockchain back to life
feed.summary: Aptos Labs, a startup founded by former employees of Meta's Diem blockchain project, has raised $200 million in strategic funding led by Andreessen Horowitz. The company aims to develop a safe and scalable blockchain network, learning from Diem's regulatory challenges. Aptos is building its own open-source blockchain for Web3 applications and expects to launch its public mainnet in the third quarter of 2022.

feed.title: ProShares Launches Metaverse ETF, Expands Innovative Fund Lineup to the Internet’s Next Frontier
feed.summary: ProShares has launched a new Metaverse ETF (VERS) designed to offer investors access to companies at the forefront of the metaverse's發展. The ETF tracks the Solactive Metaverse Theme Index, which includes 40 companies across various industries, from device makers to social media platforms. This initiative builds on ProShares' history of product innovation, including the first bitcoin-linked ETF, and aims to capitalize on the metaverse's potential to revolutionize industries.

feed.title: Why banks and NATO are worrying about a future ‘Quantum attack’
feed.summary: The article discusses the growing concern among banks and organizations like NATO about the potential for "quantum attacks" as quantum computing technology advances. Andersen Cheng, CEO of Post Quantum, warns that powerful quantum computers capable of cracking current encryption methods may be closer than initially thought, posing a significant threat to critical communications, financial data, and cryptocurrencies. The piece highlights how various nations are investing heavily in quantum technology and the commercial sector is beginning to prepare for this shift.

feed.title: The Impact of Design on the Employee Experience
feed.summary: Workday's Chief Design Officer, Jeff Gelfuso, emphasizes the importance of delivering seamless and engaging end-to-end experiences for employees within enterprise software, mirroring consumer software expectations. He discusses how Workday is achieving this through simplification, personalization, connectedness, and data-driven insights. The article highlights key design principles and Workday's initiatives like Engage, Everywhere, and Empower to improve the employee experience.

feed.title: Facebook Continues To Lose Out On User Time; Netherlands Data Center Plans Face Opposition
feed.summary: Meta Platforms (NASDAQ: FB) is experiencing a decline in user engagement on Facebook, as reported by BuzzFeed CEO Jonah Peretti, which negatively impacts its commerce revenues. Concurrently, Meta's plans for a large data center in Zeewolde, Netherlands, are facing significant political opposition after the Leefbaar Zeewolde party, which campaigned against the project, won a majority in the local elections. This comes at a time when Meta is also dealing with internal pressure from employees affected by plunging stock prices.

feed.title: Towards The Distant Virtual World: Vitalii Vashchuk Shares Insights
feed.summary: Vitalii Vashchuk, Director and Gaming Technologist at EPAM Systems, shared his insights on the metaverse's evolution and the underlying technologies. He describes the metaverse as a concept aimed at enhancing communication and experiences, offering greater freedom than Web2.0. Key technologies enabling the metaverse include Blockchain, NFTs, AI, and IoT.

feed.title: Brookfield agrees to buy Hibernia REIT for $1.2 billion
feed.summary: Brookfield Asset Management Inc. has reached an agreement to acquire Hibernia REIT Plc for approximately 1.09 billion euros ($1.2 billion) in cash, causing Hibernia's shares to surge to a record high. The deal, which offers a 33.9% premium over Hibernia's average share price, sees Brookfield expanding its real estate portfolio in Dublin, a market where tech giants are rapidly growing. Brookfield is actively investing in European office landlords, capitalizing on market uncertainty and discounts to asset values.

feed.title: Amazon Stock Rally Erases Losses for the Year
feed.summary: Amazon.com Inc. shares rallied, becoming the first megacap tech stock to recover its losses for the year,

feed.title: Vietnam says over 3,200 "toxic" social media posts removed in Q1
feed.summary: Vietnam's information ministry announced that social media platforms removed over 3,200 "toxic" posts and videos in the first quarter of the year at the government's request. This action is part of Vietnam's ongoing efforts to control online content, with companies like Facebook, YouTube, and TikTok complying with requests to take down content deemed false, offensive, or anti-state. The ruling Communist Party maintains strict media censorship, and new internet laws have raised concerns about potential crackdowns on dissent.

feed.title: Meta to open new engineering hub in Toronto, expects to create 2,500 jobs
feed.summary: Meta Platforms Inc. is establishing a new engineering hub in Toronto, aiming to create up to 2,500 high-tech jobs focused on immersive online experiences and the metaverse. These roles will offer both in-office and remote work options, making them accessible to Canadians nationwide. Additionally, Meta will invest $510,000 in grants for Canadian research labs to foster metaverse-related innovations.

feed.title: Silicon Ranch, TVA, Meta break ground on 70MW solar facility in Tennessee
feed.summary: Silicon Ranch, the Tennessee Valley Authority (TVA), and Meta have commenced construction on the new 70MW McKellar Solar Farm in Madison County, Tennessee. This facility, part of TVA's Green Invest program, aims to supply 100% clean energy to support Meta’s regional operations. Silicon Ranch will invest over $90 million in the project, which is expected to create over 350 construction jobs and be completed by the end of the year.

feed.title: TVA & Silicon Ranch break ground on 70MW solar farm serving Meta’s Tennessee campus
feed.summary: Ground has been broken on a new 70MW solar farm in Madison County, Tennessee, a collaboration between the Tennessee Valley Authority (TVA), Meta, the Jackson Energy Authority (JEA), and Silicon Ranch. This McKellar Solar Farm will supply 100 percent renewable energy to Meta's Gallatin data centers upon its expected completion by the end of 2022. Silicon Ranch will fund, own, and operate the facility, investing over $90 million in its construction.

feed.title: Financial Firm MetaBank Rebrands as Pathward
feed.summary: MetaBank, a financial empowerment company, announced its rebranding to Pathward, unifying the company under a single identity after strategic acquisitions and a brand strategy review in 2021. The new name, Pathward, signifies the company's commitment to providing "a path forward to people and businesses" and expanding financial access for the unbanked, underbanked, and underserved. Its public holding company, Meta Financial Group, will also change its name to Pathward Financial by the end of 2022, a move further emphasized by Facebook's recent rebranding to Meta and its acquisition of Meta Financial's trademark assets.

feed.title: Facebook advertisers can pursue class action over ad rates
feed.summary: A U.S. judge has ruled that a lawsuit accusing Meta Platforms Inc.'s Facebook of deceiving advertisers about its "potential reach" tool can proceed as a class action. This decision allows potentially millions of advertisers to sue as a group, alleging that Facebook inflated advertising reach and charged artificially high premiums for ad placements. The lawsuit claims that even senior Facebook executives were aware of the inflated metrics but took no action.

feed.title: MetaBank announces name change
feed.summary: MetaBank announced its new name will be Pathward, following the sale of its existing name and trademark assets to Facebook's parent company, Meta, for $60 million in December. The full transition to Pathward, including a new brand identity and website, is expected by the end of the calendar year, with its public holding company also changing to Pathward Financial, Inc. CEO Brett Pharr stated the name change reflects the company's commitment to financial inclusion and removing barriers for the unbanked, underbanked, and underserved.

feed.title: North America PV News Snippets
feed.summary: Nextracker will supply its bifacial optimized solar trackers and TrueCapture technology for the 450 MW first phase of the 1.5 GW Sudair Solar PV Plant in Saudi Arabia. SunPower's SunVault Storage now offers whole-home backup with 26 kWh and 52 kWh configurations and a 10-year warranty. DESRI commissioned two solar plants totaling 189 MW in Michigan, while Silicon Ranch began construction on a 70 MW AC solar project in Tennessee for Meta. Enphase Energy partnered with Green Mountain Power for a battery lease grid services pilot program and is launching its Grid Services Manager.

feed.title: 3 Tech Trends Emerge for Investors
feed.summary: Morgan Stanley's TMT Conference identified three major technology trends for investors: the metaverse, M&A in tech, and FinTech payment systems. The metaverse is creating new monetizable digital assets and opportunities for brands, while increased corporate interest and market volatility are driving M&A. FinTech is expanding with embedded financial services, cross-border payments, and digital wallets, opening new avenues for financial services across various industries.

feed.title: DoubleLine Shiller CAPE US Equities ETF ETF Price, Holdings, & News (NYSEARCA:DCPE)
feed.summary: The DoubleLine Shiller CAPE US Equities ETF (NYSEARCA:DCPE) was launched on March 31, 2022, and is an actively managed ETF aiming to outperform the S&P 500 Index by investing in undervalued US stocks chosen based on the CAPE ratio and momentum factors. As of May 2026, its stock was trading at $32.46 with assets under management of $33.11 million and a net expense ratio of 0.65%. The ETF's top holdings include Meta Platforms, Linde, and Alphabet.
